recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-18639 unless a future editorial pass wants to revisit terminology wording more broadly.
issue_request: FHIR-18639 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 vocab change request asking that wording saying each code system can have one or more properties be clarified to say a code system may define one or more concept properties, because the properties apply to concepts rather than to the code system itself.
initial_application: The Jira comment identifies git 66ae1e40f1bc02283363c872db14035fc795f8f7. That commit changed source/codesystem/codesystem-notes.xml from "Each code system can have one or more properties" to "Each code system can define one or more concept properties" and made the same concept-property wording change in the then-current codesystem spreadsheet source. Later source refactoring removed source/codesystem/codesystem-spreadsheet.xml and carried the active definitions into source/codesystem/structuredefinition-CodeSystem.xml.
additional_context: CodeSystem is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini. The current CodeSystem introduction distinguishes code-system-level properties from concept properties, the narrative section is now headed "Concept Properties" and says each code system can define concept properties, and CodeSystem.property is defined as additional information about each concept. Searches for FHIR-18639 in Zulip and Confluence found no community record that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope CodeSystem source already preserves the approved distinction between properties of the code system resource itself and concept properties defined by a code system for its concepts.
